title: Psychometric Validation of the Training Needs Assessment Tool (TNAT-38)
author: Eman Zaid Almaazmi

Statistical Software and Code Sharing Objective: Ensure reproducibility through transparent software specification and open-access code. Procedure: Primary software platforms: - R (lavaan ≥0.6-10 for CFA; psych, EFAtools for EFA; lordif, difR for DIF; irr, semTools for reliability) - Mplus (version 8.3+ for sensitivity/alternative model testing) Data analysis code: - Fully annotated R code for all steps (EFA, CFA, MGCFA, DIF) - Reproducibility: Code runs identically on any machine with proper packages installed - Test cases: Synthetic dataset for code validation Code availability: - Upload to Open Science Framework ([osf.io/xwyk3]( https://osf.io/xwyk3)) and/or Zenodo community ([zenodo.org/communities/lhs]( https://zenodo.org/communities/lhs)) - Published as supplementary material with companion manuscript - DOI and citation provided for code attribution Success Criteria: All analysis code published with the manuscript; reproducibility verified on an independent system

steps.title: Define Study Design and Sample
steps.instruction: Establish a cross-sectional psychometric validation study with a prospective test-retest subsample.

substeps.instruction: Recruit a total sample of N=412 adults (≥18 years) providing care to persons ≥60 years with ≥3 months experience, fluent in Arabic or English, excluding those with severe cognitive impairment.

Implement stratified sampling across eight caregiver types (T1–T8): Home health aide, in-home personal care attendant, hospital patient care assistant, long-term care facility nursing assistant, dementia care specialist, care coordinator/supervisor, palliative care assistant, and community health worker/volunteer, targeting n=50–65 per type.
Recruit a test-retest subsample of N=79 (20% systematic recruitment) at Month 1, with a 14-day interval; exclude participants if role, employment, or care recipient status changes.

Ensure recruitment across six UAE site types: long-term care facilities, private home care agencies, government healthcare, NGOs, caregiver training institutes, and hospital geriatric units in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and Sharjah.

steps.title: Specify and Administer TNAT-38 Instrument
steps.instruction: Prepare and administer the 38-item TNAT-38 instrument across seven competency domains (CD1–CD7).

substeps.instruction: Organize items by domain: CD1: Personal Care & Safety (6 items), CD2: Health Monitoring & Medication Management (6 items), CD3: Communication & Interpersonal Skills (6 items), CD4: Care Coordination & Navigation (5 items), CD5: Emotional Resilience & Self-Care (5 items), CD6: Cultural Competence & Ethical Awareness (4 items), and CD7: Digital Literacy & Technology Use (6 items).
Utilize a dual-scale system: Importance scale (1–5: Not Important to Extremely Important) and Competency scale (1–5: Not Competent to Highly Competent).
Calculate Gap scores as Importance minus Competency (range -4 to +4).
Ensure availability in Arabic and English (with Tagalog, Nepali, and Somali translations in progress) following ISPOR 12-step guidelines.
Administer via bilingual coordinators using paper or tablets via REDCap, with a total time of ~30 minutes (demographics 5 min, TNAT-38 15 min, CSES-10 3 min, ZBI-12 3 min).

steps.title: Perform Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA)
steps.instruction: Determine if the seven-factor structure emerges naturally using R `psych` and `EFAtools` packages.

substeps.instruction: Use principal axis factoring with oblimin rotation and polychoric correlation matrices for ordinal Likert data.
Conduct parallel analysis comparing observed eigenvalues to the 95th percentile of 1,000 random eigenvalues to determine factor retention.
Test both the 4-factor solution (predicted by statistical criteria) and the pre-specified 7-factor model (expert consensus).
Verify polychoric correlation matrix condition (target condition number <20, no singularity) and report any Heywood cases.

steps.title: Perform Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA)
steps.instruction: Confirm the seven-factor structure using an independent Phase 1 sample (n=206) with WLSMV estimation and polychoric correlations.

substeps.instruction: Specify the model with seven correlated factors (CD1–CD7), 38 observed items, delta parameterization, and the first item per domain loading set to 1.0.
Test three candidate models: Model 1 (Correlated 7-factor), Model 2 (Higher-order factor), and Model 3 (Bifactor).
Evaluate fit using thresholds: RMSEA < 0.06, CFI ≥ 0.95, and SRMR < 0.05 (or as specified in the Go/No-Go protocol).
If fit is poor, examine the top 5 modification indices; allow correlated residuals only within domains if theoretically justified.
Conduct sensitivity analysis comparing WLSMV vs. robust MLR (target ΔCFI < 0.002).

steps.title: Conduct Multi-Level Measurement Invariance Testing
steps.instruction: Ensure the TNAT-38 measures equivalent constructs across language, caregiver type, and healthcare contexts using Multi-group CFA (MGCFA).

substeps.instruction: Level 1 (Language): Test Arabic, English, and other translations (min n=30/group) through configural, metric, and scalar invariance (threshold ΔCFI ≤ 0.01).
Level 2 (Caregiver Type): Test eight T1–T8 types (min n=25/type) or collapsed Formal vs. Informal (threshold ΔCFI ≤ 0.015).
Level 3 (Healthcare Context): Test Institutional vs. Community settings (min n=50/group) for configural and metric invariance (ΔCFI ≤ 0.01).
Apply Partial Invariance Protocol if ΔCFI exceeds thresholds: use backward deletion of non-invariant constraints (highest modification index first) until ΔCFI ≤ threshold.

steps.title: Analyze Differential Item Functioning (DIF)
steps.instruction: Identify measurement bias across subgroups using the R `lordif` package (primary) and `difR` package (secondary).

substeps.instruction: Stratify by Literacy/Education (Low: Secondary vs. High: Secondary+) and Caregiver Type (Formal vs. Informal or T1–T8 pairwise).
Apply Logistic Regression (Lord's approach): logit(P(Yij = 1)) = β₀ + β₁(Total Score) + β₂(Group) + β₃(Total Score × Group).
Report Uniform DIF (β₂), Non-uniform DIF (β₃), Nagelkerke ΔR², and Mantel-Haenszel-scaled DIF.
Correct for multiple testing using Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at q < 0.13.

steps.title: Establish Internal Consistency and Reliability
steps.instruction: Evaluate reliability for the full sample (n=412) and test-retest subsample (n=79) using R `psych`, `irr`, and `semTools` packages.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Cronbach's α (target ≥0.80 total, ≥0.70 per domain) and McDonald's ω (omega-total and omega-hierarchical).
Verify item-total correlations (r ≥ 0.30 per item).
Calculate ICC(2,1) for test-retest stability at 14 days (target ≥0.75 total, ≥0.70 per domain).
Exclude test-retest participants who reported major changes in role, employment, or care recipient status.

steps.title: Validate Convergent and Discriminant Validity
steps.instruction: Establish relationships between TNAT-38 and other validated measures.

substeps.instruction: Test convergent validity: Correlate TNAT-38 competency scores with CSES-10 (Caregiver Self-Efficacy Scale) targeting r ≥ 0.40.
Test discriminant validity: Correlate TNAT-38 gap scores with ZBI-12 (Caregiver Burden Scale) targeting r < 0.30.
Perform subgroup analysis by caregiver type and language group to ensure consistency.

steps.title: Execute Go/No-Go Decision Protocol
steps.instruction: Convene a Decision Committee (Psychometrics Lead, Trial Methodology Lead, PI, and Lead Statistician) to determine if TNAT-38 can be the primary outcome for RCTs.

substeps.instruction: Scenario A (Green): Proceed if CFA fit is optimal (RMSEA < 0.06, CFI ≥ 0.95, SRMR < 0.05), scalar invariance is achieved for Language and Type, and DIF is minimal.
Scenario B (Amber): Require minor item revision and targeted re-validation (n=50–75) if partial invariance is found (3–4 items non-invariant per domain).
Scenario C (Red): Reject as primary outcome if CFA fit is poor (RMSEA > 0.08, CFI < 0.90), significant non-invariance exists, or substantial DIF is present.
Scenario D (Red-Alt): Approve for RCTs only with mandatory stratified analysis by caregiver type and domain-specific scoring.
